**TL;DR: Didn't pay electric bill, power got disconnected, woke up late for work, PS4 might be fucked.**

Alright this actually happened *yesterday* but I don't think anyone really cares. So you know how it goes. Money gets tight, or procrastinate on paying your bills, money gets even more tight and then you can't pay your bills. Well, I actually straight up forgot about my electric bill somehow and my power got turned off. This, of course, meant my alarm clock didn't go off in the morning, causing me to oversleep (because I make bad decisions at night, like staying up late playing PS4).

Woke up, realized I was late, and rushed to work. Luckily the manager didn't really seem to give much of a shit, he mostly just seemed relieved that I didn't no-call no-show (we've had one other person do that this week, and another employee just put in their two weeks). When I got home, though, I went to turn on my PS4.

"PS4 could not start." Well, fuck.

Turns out that since I had left my PS4 on all night (another bad decision), it decided to go and install that handy dandy update they published a couple of days ago. Well, my power got cut off in the middle of that update, so now my PS4 is stuck in limbo. It's telling me to download the system update on a thumb drive and plug it in. Well, I did that, and it still didn't work. Called customer service and found out that because my thumb drive is 32gb, the system is interpreting it as an external hard drive rather than a thumb drive; the distinction between the two apparently actually matters for this particular operation. Kind of weird, and honestly sounds kind of like bullshit, but the guy recommended a 4gb thumb stick instead, so I'm going to go out and buy one tomorrow and see what happens.

I know the PS4 is out of warranty, and the customer service rep informed me that the operation might not work, and if it did, there was still a chance I would lose all of my save data. Which would fucking blow, because there's thousands of hours of accumulated save data on that machine thanks to everyone in the household who uses it. Just hoping at this point that my PS4 hasn't become a paperweight.
TIFU by not paying my electric bill.

Hi there. I fix these and other things for a living. Have a go at this..

PS4: How to get into Safe Mode / Factory Reset

  1. Power off the PS4 by holding down the power button for several seconds. You will hear a beep and see the power light turn red.

  2. Power on the PS4 by holding the power button down and keeping it held down. You will hear an initial beep when you press the power button. Wait about 7 seconds until you hear a second beep.

  3. Once you hear the second beep, release the power button and the Safe Mode screens should appear. You will need to connect your DualShock 4 controller via a USB cable to the PS4 since Bluetooth is not active when in Safe Mode.

You will have the following options in safe mode:

Restart System – Exits Safe Mode and restarts the PlayStation 4 back into the XMB.
Change Resolution – Changes the screen resolution to 480p when the PlayStation 4 is restarted.
Update System Software – Allows the PlayStation 4 to update the system software via Internet, USB Drive, or Disc.
Restore Default Settings – Restores the PlayStation 4 to the default factory settings.
Rebuild Database – Scans the drive and creates a new database of all content.
This operation may take a long time depending on the type and number of data items.
Initialize PS4 – All data and settings will be lost by performing this step. 
Initialize PS4 (Reinstall System Software) – This deletes all information on the HDD including the System Software.

Try Rebuild Database first. If that doesn't work, give Initialize PS4 a try. These fix the majority of PlayStation issues I see.
